paragraphs: My name is Lily, and I am ten years old. On Saturday morning, Tom and I woke up late. There was a note on the fridge. It was from Dad. It said, "Good morning! We have no milk and no eggs. Please go to the market with Tom. Walk north to the corner of the street. Then walk east to the market. The woman at the blue shop sells milk and eggs. The money is in the red box on the table. Thank you, Dad."

Tom read the note two times. "North first," he said. "Which way is north?" I asked. "The sun comes up in the east," said Tom. "When we walk north, the east is on our right." We took the money from the red box. Pip came with us, and he walked in front. We walked north on our street to the corner. Then we turned right and walked east.

The market was busy, and we saw the blue shop. "Do you have any eggs?" I asked the woman. "Yes, we do," she said. "Is there any milk too?" asked Tom. "Yes, here you are," she said. She gave us a box of eggs and a bottle of milk. We said thank you and walked home. Pip walked next to us this time.

At home, we put the milk and the eggs in the fridge. Then Tom wrote a note under Dad's note. It said, "We went to the market. The milk and the eggs are in the fridge. We are in the garden." Later, Dad wrote one more line. "Excellent work, you two!" A note on the fridge tells us who, what, and where.
text.summary: Dad leaves a note on the fridge. Lily and Tom follow it to the market, buy milk and eggs, and leave a note for Dad.
